name: Imroing
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Babar Islands; only survey wordlists (Taber 1993 SW Maluku survey), no phonological description

sources.citation: LexiRumah 3 (Kaiping, Edwards & Klamer), lect imro1237 'Imroing', 189 forms from Taber 1993 with Owen Edwards' preliminary phonemic analysis; https://github.com/lessersunda/lexirumah-data (cldf/)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Wordlist only; stress marked (IPA ˈ) on all 189 forms as in Taber. My tabulation of Taber's marks: 154 penultimate, 24 antepenultimate (mostly stems + suffix -e/-nu/-mu, e.g. ˈilijɛʔ sand, ˈloronu sea, iˈririje tail), 2 pre-antepenultimate (ˈululije mountain, ˈatitije mosquito), 2 final (woˈru two, woˈlim five), 7 monosyllables. Data, not a statement.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Owen Edwards. 2026. The Austronesian languages of eastern Indonesia and Timor-Leste: Unravelling their prehistory and classification. Berlin: Language Science Press (book 526), 948 pp. CC BY.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Section 4.6.5 Babar (pp. 223 ff.) states Taber (1993) is the only data source for Imroing and re-transcribes it; no statement about Imroing stress anywhere in the Babar section. Only a general regional remark, p. 115: 'While penultimate stress is the normal rule for Wallacean languages, words with penultimate schwa can have stress on other syllables.' Also p. 202: SW Maluku sound change 'Unstressed non-final vowels were then usually lost' (proto-level).

sources.citation: Edwards, Owen. 2023a. Emplawas and languages of the Babar islands. Endangered Languages Archive (ELAR) deposit IPF0417, hdl 2196/28f40694-81ac-4d06-b515-617dd6469394
sources.note: Deposit page lists Imroing among 13 languages with 9-10 Imroing items (wordlists, paradigms, recordings, grammar notes; mostly open access). Item-level files could not be reached through the site's facet interface; deposit-level metadata says nothing about stress.

sources.citation: Zobel, Erik. 2018 [first posted 2014]. The South Babar languages of Southwest Maluku. Working paper, https://ezlinguistics.blogspot.com/p/south-babar.html
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Historical phonology of South Babar (incl. Imroing) built on Taber 1993. Stress mentioned only for proto-forms ('In stressed (= penultimate) position, all four vowels remain distinct'; 'Stressed *u underwent a split in Proto South Babar'); no synchronic statement on Imroing stress.

sources.citation: Steinhauer, Hein. 2009. The sounds of Southeast Babar. In K. Alexander Adelaar & Andrew Pawley (eds), Austronesian historical linguistics and culture history: a festschrift for Robert Blust (Pacific Linguistics 601), 91-105. Canberra: ANU. Open access, hdl 1885/34582.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: SISTER LANGUAGE, NOT IMROING: Southeast Babar / Letwurung (sout2883, [vbb]). p. 96: 'Stress does not seem to be phonemic at the word level. Often the same word occurs with different stress in comparable environments. Below I refrain with some exceptions from indicating stress.' fn. 26 (p. 102): one set of possessive enclitics 'always clearly attracted phrasal stress'. Nothing on Imroing stress (Imroing mentioned only in the language inventory, pp. 92-94).

sources.citation: ABVD language 316 'Imroing' (typed by S. Greenhill from Taber 1993), Austronesian Basic Vocabulary Database, https://abvd.eva.mpg.de/austronesian/language.php?id=316
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Wordlist only: 122 items, every item carries Taber's stress mark (e.g. 'kenah walk, o'kamu head, lim'mute hand, 'rulije bone, wo'ru two). No prose statement.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid imro1237; Wikipedia 'Imroing language' and 'Babar languages'; Glottolog reference 110693
sources.note: Glottolog lists only Taber 1993 (p. 393) and Taber 1996 (pp. 119-121), both for subclassification; no descriptive references. Wikipedia stub, no phonology.

sources.note: Sole primary source with Imroing data; the wordlists mark stress on every Imroing item, so the introductory transcription notes (pp. ~400-404) are the one place a published remark on Imroing/South Babar stress placement is likely to exist. Also the source behind ABVD 316, LexiRumah, Zobel 2018 and Grimes & Edwards 2026.
